sourceEnglishObjective: Deliver the same news to a crew member, a homeowner, your manager and an inspector in the right register
sourceEnglishSpeaking: You are the crew lead and the AI will play the people you work with, one after another: tell each of them that you found rotten deck, switching between tú and usted and using softeners like quisiera and me gustaría.

examples.es: Disculpe, señora; quisiera comentarle algo que encontramos.
examples.en: Excuse me, ma'am; I'd like to mention something we found.

example.target: ¿Le hablo de usted o de tú?
example.native: Should I address you as usted or tú?

sourceVerbExamples.note: Hablarle de usted means to address someone as usted; hablarle de tú, as tú.

example.target: Kevin quiere saber cómo hablar con cada persona.
example.native: Kevin wants to know how to talk to each person.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Softener: quisiera (I would like) is more polite than quiero.

example.native: Would you allow me to show you the area?

sourceVerbExamples.note: The conditional works as a softener: ¿me permitiría…?

example.target: Rogelio le muestra las fotos al gerente.
example.native: Rogelio shows the photos to the manager.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Stem change o to ue: muestro, but mostramos.

example.target: El mensaje es el mismo, pero el tono cambia según la persona.
example.native: The message is the same, but the tone changes depending on the person.
